title: Dark Synth: A Tag-Audited Methodology for Mathematical Work, with a Kernel-Verified Catalytic Pass Barrier
description:
Dark Synth is a tag-audited methodology for mathematical work: every claim carries a two-axis [source/status] tag, every correction is logged in an append-only hash-chained ledger, every [run] claim is kernel-accepted with a recorded sha256, and the audit trail is tested against its own mutants.

The reference vault (vault/catalytic_barrier/) contains:

  • Theorem 3.6 — for the interpolation class Cint, any linear-extraction catalytic algorithm requires at least D+1 evaluation passes. Kernel-verified in Coq 8.18 (Closed under the global context).
  • Theorem 3.7 — the same boundary-projection adversary holds over any commutative ring with 1 ≠ 0, including Zm with zero divisors. Kernel-verified in Lean 4.7.0 (#print axioms yields [propext, Quot.sound]).
  • Audit drawer A1–A5 with a mutation matrix naming which corrections are mechanized and which are hand-audit-only.
  • Failure-mode catalog FM1–FM14, each recording a bug the methodology caught in its own construction.

Code is MIT-licensed; documentation and prose are CC BY 4.0. The ledger head is anchored to Bitcoin via OpenTimestamps.
